terms.gloss: go beyond, exceed (a number, a measure)
terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, transitive in this sense
evidence: Suet. Tib. 68: statūra quae jūstam excēderet (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Its main sense is “go out, leave”; with an accusative of a number, an age or a measure (modum excēdere) it is “exceed”, from Livy on.

terms.gloss: surpass, be greater than; (intransitive) be more than enough
evidence: Liv. 9.32.7: numerō hostis, virtūte Rōmānus superat (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Par. 49: cui dēest an cui superat? (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: To be greater than another in something (ablative); also to defeat. Used absolutely, it means “be in excess, be left over”.

evidence: Plin. NH 18.168: Nīlus exsuperāvit sēdecim cubita (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Mostly poetic and post-Augustan; of a level or a measure passed (a river over its mark).

phrases.latin: Modum nē excesserīs: duo crustula satis sunt.
phrases.english: Don’t overdo it: two biscuits are enough.

sources: Lewis & Short: excedo · Lewis & Short: supero · Lewis & Short: exsupero
The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 109.
